title: United Nations: Organs, Agencies, Programmes & Funds

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the principal organs of the United Nations:
1. The Trusteeship Council suspended its operations in 1994 after the last Trust Territory, Palau, became independent.
2. The International Court of Justice is the only principal organ not located in New York.
3. The Secretary-General is elected by the Security Council alone.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Trusteeship Council's work was done once all Trust Territories reached self-rule, so it suspended operations on 1 Nov 1994. The ICJ sits at the Peace Palace, The Hague. The Secretary-General is appointed by the General Assembly on the Security Council's recommendation (Art 97), not by the Council alone.
questions.h: Six organs, one lives in The Hague: ICJ.

questions.q:
Consider the following organisations:
1. International Atomic Energy Agency
2. International Fund for Agricultural Development
3. United Nations Industrial Development Organization
4. World Trade Organization
How many of the above are specialised agencies of the United Nations?
questions.e: IFAD and UNIDO are specialised agencies. The IAEA and the WTO are 'related organisations': they work with the UN but are not specialised agencies under Arts 57 and 63, and the IAEA reports to both the General Assembly and the Security Council.
questions.s: un.org, UN System chart; UN Charter Arts 57, 63

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about voting in the UN Security Council:
1. An abstention by a permanent member does not prevent the adoption of a substantive resolution.
2. Procedural matters are decided by an affirmative vote of nine members and are not subject to veto.
3. The non-permanent members are elected by the Security Council itself.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 27 requires nine affirmative votes for all decisions, with the concurring votes of the permanent members only on non-procedural matters; practice treats abstention as non-concurrence that is not a veto. The ten non-permanent members are elected by the General Assembly (two-thirds majority), not by the Council.

questions.q:
Statement-I: A resolution of the Security Council adopted under Chapter VII of the UN Charter is binding on all member states.
Statement-II: Under Article 25 of the Charter, members agree to accept and carry out the decisions of the Security Council.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The binding force of Council decisions comes from Article 25, where members agree to accept and carry them out. General Assembly resolutions, by contrast, are generally recommendatory.

questions.q:
Match List-I (ECOSOC Regional Commission) with List-II (Headquarters):
List-I
A. Economic Commission for Africa
B. Economic and Social Commission for Western Asia
C. Economic Commission for Latin America and the Caribbean
D. Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific
List-II
1. Santiago
2. Bangkok
3. Beirut
4. Addis Ababa
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: ECA is in Addis Ababa, ESCWA in Beirut, ECLAC in Santiago and ESCAP in Bangkok. The fifth commission, ECE, is in Geneva.
questions.h: ECA = Addis, ESCWA = Beirut, ECLAC = Santiago, ESCAP = Bangkok.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the International Court of Justice:
1. It has 15 judges elected for nine-year terms, with one-third of the seats renewed every three years.
2. In the election of judges, permanent members of the Security Council hold a veto.
3. No two judges may be nationals of the same State.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Judges are elected concurrently by the General Assembly and the Security Council, each needing an absolute majority, and the Statute says no distinction is made between permanent and non-permanent members, so there is no veto. Staggered terms ensure continuity, and the nationality bar keeps the bench diverse.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the International Court of Justice is correct?
o: Individuals and corporations may bring contentious cases before it.
Only States may be parties to contentious cases, while certain UN organs and agencies may seek advisory opinions.
Its judgments are enforced directly by the General Assembly.
questions.e: Article 34 of the Statute says only States may be parties in cases before the Court; advisory opinions can be requested by the General Assembly, the Security Council and other organs or agencies authorised by the Assembly. If a party fails to comply, the other may go to the Security Council (Art 94), not the Assembly. The seat is the Peace Palace, The Hague.
questions.s: ICJ Statute Art 34; UN Charter Arts 94, 96

questions.q:
With reference to the Kulbhushan Jadhav case before the International Court of Justice (judgment of 17 July 2019), consider the following statements:
1. The Court found that Pakistan had breached its obligations under Article 36 of the Vienna Convention on Consular Relations.
2. The Court ordered the immediate release of Jadhav.
3. The Court required Pakistan to provide effective review and reconsideration of his conviction and sentence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The ICJ held that Pakistan violated consular access rights under Art 36 and directed effective review and reconsideration of the conviction and sentence. It did not annul the verdict or order release, which is why statement 2 is wrong.
questions.s: ICJ judgment, India v. Pakistan, 17 July 2019

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Security Council:
1. It has been enlarged only once, in 1965.
2. Before that enlargement it had six non-permanent members.
3. The enlargement required an amendment to the UN Charter.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The amendment to Article 23, which came into force in 1965, raised membership from 11 to 15 by adding four non-permanent seats; Article 27 was also amended to raise the voting threshold to nine. The permanent membership has never been enlarged.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a principal organ of the United Nations?
questions.e: Article 7 names six principal organs: General Assembly, Security Council, ECOSOC, Trusteeship Council, ICJ and Secretariat. The Peacebuilding Commission (2005) is an advisory subsidiary body of the General Assembly and the Security Council.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UN Human Rights Council:
1. It was created in 2006, replacing the Commission on Human Rights.
2. Its members are elected directly and individually by secret ballot by a majority of the members of the General Assembly.
3. It is a subsidiary organ of the Security Council.
4. A member may serve any number of consecutive terms.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Council was created by General Assembly resolution 60/251 in 2006 and elected by an absolute majority (97 of 193). It is a subsidiary body of the General Assembly, and members cannot serve more than two consecutive three-year terms.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UN Human Rights Council:
1. It has 47 members.
2. The African and Asia-Pacific groups together hold 13 seats.
3. The General Assembly may suspend a member that commits gross and systematic violations of human rights by a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Council has 47 seats and the African and Asia-Pacific groups hold 13 seats each (26 together), so statement 2 is wrong. Suspension needs a two-thirds majority of members present and voting; Libya (2011) and Russia (2022) were suspended this way.

questions.q: The Universal Periodic Review conducted under the UN Human Rights Council is best described as
o: a peer review of the human rights record of all UN member states, carried out periodically
a review limited to the human rights record of the Council's 47 members
a judicial process in which the ICJ examines human rights complaints
a mechanism that imposes economic sanctions on states violating human rights
questions.e: The UPR, created along with the Council in 2006, reviews every UN member state in turn, using state-to-state recommendations. It is a cooperative peer-review process, not a court and not a sanctions regime.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India and the UN Security Council:
1. India's most recent term as a non-permanent member was 2021-22.
2. India held the monthly presidency of the Council in August 2021 and December 2022.
3. India did not serve on the Council during the 1990s.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: India served in 2021-22, its eighth term, and held the presidency in August 2021 and December 2022. It also served in 1991-92, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: MEA / un.org, India at the UN Security Council 2021-22

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the proposals for reform of the UN Security Council:
1. The G4 group consists of India, Brazil, Germany and Italy.
2. The Ezulwini Consensus is the African Union's common position demanding at least two permanent seats for Africa.
3. The Uniting for Consensus group, in which Italy and Pakistan are prominent, opposes the creation of new permanent seats.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The G4 is India, Brazil, Germany and Japan, not Italy; Italy is a leading member of the opposing Uniting for Consensus group. The Ezulwini Consensus (2005) is the African Union position seeking at least two permanent seats with veto rights.
questions.h: G4 = Japan, not Italy. Italy leads the rival 'Coffee Club'.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The UN Environment Programme is headquartered in Nairobi.
Statement-II: UNEP was established following the 1972 United Nations Conference on the Human Environment held at Stockholm.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Both statements are true: UNEP is based in Nairobi and was created by the General Assembly in December 1972 after the Stockholm Conference. The Stockholm origin does not explain why its seat is in Nairobi.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The International Court of Justice can adjudicate a dispute between a State and a multinational corporation.
Statement-II: Only States may be parties to contentious cases before the Court.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Article 34 of the ICJ Statute allows only States to be parties in contentious cases. So the Court cannot decide a dispute involving a corporation, which makes Statement-I wrong.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Traditional UN peacekeeping missions are authorised by the Security Council.
Statement-II: UN peacekeeping troops are drawn only from the armed forces of the five permanent members.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Peacekeeping mandates are set by the Security Council, but troops come from member states that volunteer them. The leading contributors have been mostly developing countries, not the permanent members, and the UN has no standing army.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about UN peacekeeping:
1. The first peacekeeping mission was the UN Truce Supervision Organization, set up in 1948.
2. Peacekeeping operations are established by the Security Council.
3. Contingents are contributed voluntarily by member states.
4. A mission is normally deployed without the consent of the host state.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: UNTSO (1948) is the oldest mission, the Council authorises operations and states provide troops voluntarily. Consent of the main parties is one of the three basic principles, along with impartiality and non-use of force except in self-defence and defence of the mandate.

questions.q: Which one of the following UN bodies was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2020?
questions.e: The Nobel Committee honoured the World Food Programme in 2020 for combating hunger and using food security as a tool against conflict. UNICEF won in 1965 and UNHCR in 1954 and 1981.

questions.q:
Match List-I (UN agency) with List-II (Headquarters):
List-I
A. International Fund for Agricultural Development
B. International Civil Aviation Organization
C. United Nations Industrial Development Organization
D. Universal Postal Union
List-II
1. Vienna
2. Rome
3. Montreal
4. Bern
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: IFAD is in Rome (as are FAO and WFP), ICAO is in Montreal, UNIDO is in Vienna and the UPU is in Bern.

questions.q:
Match List-I (UN specialised agency) with List-II (Core area of work):
List-I
A. International Maritime Organization
B. World Meteorological Organization
C. International Telecommunication Union
D. World Intellectual Property Organization
List-II
1. Intellectual property
2. Weather and climate
3. Shipping safety and prevention of marine pollution
4. Telecommunication standards and radio spectrum
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: IMO handles ship safety and marine pollution (for example MARPOL), WMO coordinates weather and climate services, ITU handles telecom standards and radio spectrum, and WIPO deals with intellectual property.

questions.q:
Arrange the following UN bodies in the chronological order of their establishment:
1. UN Environment Programme
2. UN Children's Fund
3. UN Development Programme
4. UN Women
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: UNICEF came first (December 1946, for post-war child relief), then UNDP (1965, merging two earlier programmes), UNEP (1972, after Stockholm) and UN Women (2010, merging four earlier entities).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC):
1. It has 54 members elected by the General Assembly for three-year terms.
2. Its decisions require a two-thirds majority of members present and voting.
3. It may grant consultative status to non-governmental organisations.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: ECOSOC has 54 members, each with one vote, and decides by a simple majority of those present and voting (Art 67), so statement 2 is wrong. Article 71 lets it consult NGOs, which is the basis of consultative status.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a functional commission of the Economic and Social Council?
questions.e: The Commission on Narcotic Drugs, with the Commission on the Status of Women and the Statistical Commission, is a functional commission of ECOSOC. The ILC and the Human Rights Council are subsidiary bodies of the General Assembly.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a specialised agency of the United Nations?
o: United Nations Conference on Trade and Development
questions.e: UNCTAD is a permanent organ of the General Assembly created in 1964, so it is not a specialised agency. FAO, IMO and WIPO are specialised agencies with their own constitutions and membership.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. UNEP was established by the General Assembly after the 1972 Stockholm Conference.
2. UNDP and UNICEF are specialised agencies of the United Nations.
3. UN Women was created in 2010 by merging four existing UN entities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: UNDP and UNICEF are funds and programmes created by the General Assembly, not specialised agencies, which have their own treaties and budgets. UN Women merged DAW, INSTRAW, OSAGI and UNIFEM.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UN High Commissioner for Refugees:
1. UNHCR was established by the General Assembly in 1950.
2. The 1951 Refugee Convention contains the principle of non-refoulement.
3. India is a party to the 1951 Refugee Convention.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: UNHCR was created in December 1950 and the 1951 Convention bars returning refugees to places where they face persecution. India is not a party to the 1951 Convention or its 1967 Protocol.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the World Health Organization:
1. Its Constitution entered into force on 7 April 1948, which is observed as World Health Day.
2. Its Director-General is appointed by the Security Council.
3. The World Health Assembly, in which all member states are represented, is its supreme decision-making body.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Director-General is appointed by the World Health Assembly on the nomination of the Executive Board, not by the Security Council. The Assembly meets annually in Geneva and sets WHO policy.

questions.q:
Consider the following UN bodies:
1. UN Development Programme
2. UN Children's Fund
3. UN Population Fund
4. UN Women
How many of the above have their headquarters in New York?
questions.e: All four are headquartered in New York. UNEP and UN-Habitat (Nairobi), UNHCR and UNCTAD (Geneva) and WFP (Rome) are the usual non-New York bodies of this kind.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Secretary-General of the United Nations:
1. The Secretary-General is appointed by the General Assembly on the recommendation of the Security Council.
2. The Charter fixes the Secretary-General's term at five years.
3. U Thant of Burma was the first Asian to hold the office.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 97 sets the appointment procedure, so a veto in the Council can block a candidate. The Charter does not fix a term; the five-year, renewable term is established practice.

questions.q: Which Secretary-General of the United Nations was denied a second term in 1996 because of a veto by a permanent member of the Security Council?
questions.e: Boutros Boutros-Ghali of Egypt (1992-96) is the only Secretary-General to serve a single term, because the United States vetoed his re-appointment in the Security Council.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UN Charter:
1. Article 51 recognises the inherent right of individual or collective self-defence if an armed attack occurs.
2. Article 2(7) bars UN intervention in matters essentially within domestic jurisdiction but does not prejudice enforcement measures under Chapter VII.
3. Amendments take effect when adopted by two-thirds of the General Assembly and ratified by two-thirds of members, including all permanent members of the Security Council.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three match the Charter text. Article 108 gives each permanent member an effective veto over amendments through ratification, which is one reason Charter reform is so hard.

questions.q: Enforcement measures, including sanctions and the use of force, can be authorised by the Security Council under which Chapter of the UN Charter?
questions.e: Chapter VII covers action on threats to the peace, breaches of the peace and acts of aggression. Chapter VI is pacific settlement, Chapter VIII regional arrangements and Chapter XI non-self-governing territories.
questions.s: UN Charter Chapters VI, VII, VIII, XI

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the General Assembly:
1. Each member has one vote regardless of size or population.
2. Budgetary questions are decided by a simple majority of members present and voting.
3. Election of the non-permanent members of the Security Council is an 'important question' needing a two-thirds majority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 18(2) lists budgetary questions, Security Council and ECOSOC elections, admission, suspension and expulsion as important questions needing a two-thirds majority of members present and voting, so statement 2 is wrong.

questions.q: Which Main Committee of the General Assembly deals with administrative and budgetary matters?
questions.e: The Fifth Committee handles the UN budget and administration, including peacekeeping finances. The First deals with disarmament, the Second with economic and financial matters, the Third with social and humanitarian issues, the Fourth with special political and decolonisation issues and the Sixth with legal matters.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Sustainable Development Goals:
1. The 2030 Agenda was adopted by the General Assembly in September 2015.
2. It contains 17 goals and 169 targets.
3. They replaced the Millennium Development Goals, which had ten goals.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2030 Agenda has 17 SDGs and 169 targets. The MDGs (2000) had eight goals to be met by 2015, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Pact for the Future:
1. It was adopted at the Summit of the Future held at the UN in September 2024.
2. The Global Digital Compact is annexed to it.
3. The Declaration on Future Generations is annexed to it.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Pact was adopted in September 2024 at the UN General Assembly's Summit of the Future, with the Global Digital Compact and the Declaration on Future Generations as annexes.
questions.s: un.org, Pact for the Future (22 Sep 2024)

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UN Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD):
1. It is a specialised agency of the UN.
2. It was established in 1964 as a permanent organ of the General Assembly.
3. It is headquartered in Geneva.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: UNCTAD is a General Assembly organ, not a specialised agency, set up in 1964 with a Geneva headquarters to help developing countries in trade and development.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about UNESCO:
1. Its Constitution entered into force in 1946.
2. The Convention concerning the Protection of the World Cultural and Natural Heritage (1972) was adopted by its General Conference.
3. The World Heritage List is compiled by the UN Secretary-General.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The World Heritage List is maintained by the World Heritage Committee under the 1972 Convention, not by the Secretary-General.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the International Labour Organization:
1. It was established in 1945 as part of the UN system.
2. Its headquarters is in Rome.
3. It has a tripartite structure of governments, employers and workers.
4. It received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2001.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Only statement 3 is correct. The ILO was set up in 1919 under the Treaty of Versailles, sits in Geneva, and won the Nobel Peace Prize in 1969; the UN and Kofi Annan shared the 2001 prize.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Security Council's counter-terrorism machinery:
1. Resolution 1373 (2001) set up the Counter-Terrorism Committee after the 9/11 attacks.
2. The 1267 Committee maintains a sanctions list of individuals and entities associated with ISIL (Da'esh) and Al-Qaida.
3. Names are added to the 1267 list by a simple majority vote of the General Assembly.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Committee is a Security Council body and works by consensus, so any member can place a hold on a listing proposal. The General Assembly plays no role in listing.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the General Assembly and the Security Council:
1. Under resolution 76/262 (2022), the General Assembly meets within ten working days after a veto is cast in the Security Council.
2. Under the Uniting for Peace resolution (1950), the General Assembly may consider a threat to peace when the Council fails to act for lack of unanimity of its permanent members.
3. An emergency special session of the General Assembly can be convened only on the request of the Security Council.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: An emergency special session can be called at the Council's request on a vote of any nine members, or at the request of a majority of UN members, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q: Which one of the following Indians served as the President of the International Court of Justice?
questions.e: Nagendra Singh was a judge from 1973 and President of the ICJ from 1985 to 1988. Benegal Narsing Rau also served as a judge (1952-53) but not as President.

questions.q: Which one of the following bodies was NOT established under the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea, 1982?
o: International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea
Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf
questions.e: The Permanent Court of Arbitration at The Hague dates from the 1899 Hague Convention. The ISA (Kingston), ITLOS (Hamburg) and the CLCS were set up under UNCLOS.
questions.s: UNCLOS 1982 Parts XI, XV, Annex II; pca-cpa.org

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about India's initiatives at the United Nations:
1. The General Assembly declared 21 June as the International Day of Yoga in December 2014.
2. The General Assembly proclaimed 2023 as the International Year of Millets on India's proposal.
3. The International Day of Non-Violence is observed on 30 January.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The International Day of Non-Violence is observed on 2 October, the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, under a 2007 General Assembly resolution. 30 January is his death anniversary.

questions.q: Who was the first woman to preside over the United Nations General Assembly?
questions.e: Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit of India presided over the eighth session of the General Assembly in 1953.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UN Peacebuilding Commission:
1. It is an advisory subsidiary body of both the General Assembly and the Security Council.
2. It was established in 2005.
3. It can authorise sanctions against states emerging from conflict.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Commission was created by concurrent resolutions of the General Assembly and the Security Council in 2005 to advise on post-conflict recovery. Only the Security Council, not this advisory body, can impose sanctions.

questions.q: A draft resolution on a substantive matter in the Security Council receives 10 votes in favour, 4 abstentions (including those of two permanent members) and 1 vote against from a non-permanent member. No permanent member votes against. What is the outcome?
o: It is defeated, as a member voted against.
It is defeated, as two permanent members abstained.
It is adopted, as it has at least nine affirmative votes and no permanent member has voted against.
It is referred to the General Assembly for final approval.
questions.e: A substantive decision needs nine affirmative votes with no negative vote from a permanent member. Abstention is not a veto, and a negative vote by a non-permanent member does not block the resolution.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the founding of the United Nations:
1. The Dumbarton Oaks Conference of 1944 produced the initial proposals for the world organisation.
2. The Charter was signed at San Francisco on 26 June 1945.
3. The Charter came into force on 26 June 1945.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Charter came into force on 24 October 1945, after ratification by the five permanent members and a majority of the other signatories; that date is observed as UN Day.
questions.s: un.org (History of the UN; UN Day)
